questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I valued that there were some interesting subjects which is not available in Denmark - and then I always wanted to visit Australia for culture and exploring purposes

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I teamed up with a few students from KU back home. We rented an Airbnb for the first two weeks while looking for a place, and I would definitely say it’s much easier to find accommodation when you’re there rather than searching from home. We ended up finding our house through a platform called Flatmates.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: So much cheaper than living on campus

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many different subjects to attend

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I’d say the level varies from class to class, but overall it’s easier than at KU. The workload is higher, though, since you have to hand in more assignments throughout the semester instead of just having one final exam. On the other hand, this also means that the exam period itself is very chill.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar with lectures and then tutorials (forelæsninger og holdundervisning).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Drugs that shape society
2. Health Geography
3. Genetics, Biopower, & History
4. Dancing the Dance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
podcasts and speeches and so on for assignments/exam

I really enjoyed all of my subjects, especially Genetics, Biopower, and History. The lecturer was incredibly good and engaging. The course focused on eugenics and on how evolutionary theory has been used to justify racial hierarchies, with a strong historical perspective, including examples such as the feebleminded, Nazi ideology, and similar cases.
The lecturer is also not a big fan of traditional exams, but instead encourages creative and critical thinking. So our assignments and exams took the form of things like podcasts and speeches rather than standard sit-in exams.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I expected prices to be similar to those in Denmark, but they were actually a bit cheaper overall - not by much, but still noticeable. Meat and coffee were surprisingly cheap, while alcohol and vegetables were quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the running club and the wine club - highly recommend.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are soooo many places to go - the Great Ocean Road, the East Coast, Uluru, Tasmania, Perth/west coast, New Zealand, and so on. You’ll figure it all out once you’re there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Aussies are extremely open, easy to talk to, and very laid-back. Culturally, it’s quite similar to Denmark, so you won’t experience much of a culture shock.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them - they are (in general) very open and happy to engage with you!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The people are much less reserved than Danes, which is really lovely when you are far away from home. 

Another aspect is the Aboriginal population: some communities/many people are still affected by the country’s colonial history, so it is something to approach with respect, but also incredibly interesting to learn about.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the laid-back and outgoing people—and the camping culture, which I especially enjoyed. It’s such a nice way to experience the nature and the country.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be open-minded and adventurous, and you’ll have such a good time.
2. Time flies sooo fast, so enjoy it while you’re there - say yes to as much as possible.
3. Make sure to have some savings. Travelling and experiences will be quite expensive, and it’s much nicer not having to worry about money while you are there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The semester starts early, but that also means you finish early, so you have 2 - 3 months afterwards to just travel around before the next semester starts in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got to experience so much, and it was incredibly rewarding to try living on the other side of the world for half a year. The people I met and everything I experienced made it feel very wholesome, and it’s just an opportunity I think everyone should take while having no obligations at home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did feel homesick at times, and the 10-hour time difference means you can’t always just call home, which could be quite hard for me at least. But surround yourself with good people, you’ll be just fine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Gooo, you won't regret it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
